literature.headline_zh: 人偏肺病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人偏肺病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 共有 54 名儿童参与(RSV:22,hMPV:32)。随访1~3个月未发现交叉感染。一名 RSV 感染婴儿在出院 21 天后出现 hMPV 感染,但由于间隔时间超过了 hMPV 的已知潜伏期,因此被认为是社区获得性感染。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10342440/v1]
48.7% 的患者发生 下呼吸道感染,29.3% 的患者在 14 天时出现急性 ≥10% FEV1 下降。在 下呼吸道感染 患者中,45.9% 单独接受皮质类固醇治疗,37.8% 接受皮质类固醇加利巴韦林治疗。 [10.3390/life16081323]

总体检测率为1.7%(27/1,602),其中0–5岁儿童负担最重(3.6%),冬春季为流行高峰期;基因型从2024年的A2.2.2转变为2025年的B2(12/12 vs. 0/14;p < 0.001),且111nt_dup谱系在G蛋白位点90处(S90)几乎完全固定为丝氨酸(98.9% vs. 180nt_dup的0%;p < 0.001)。 [10.3389/fmicb.2026.1915595]
审查得出的结论是,hMPV 是全球范围内上肢和 下呼吸道感染 的主要原因。它强调缺乏获得许可的 疫苗 或特定的 抗病毒药物 疗法,支持性护理仍然是主要管理策略。 [10.3329/jmomc.v11i2.90296]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。

Lower respiratory tract infection occurred in 48.7%, and an acute ≥10% FEV1 decline at 14 days was observed in 29.3%. Among patients with lower respiratory tract infection, 45.9% received corticosteroids alone and 37.8% corticosteroids plus ribavirin. [10.3390/life16081323]

The overall detection rate was 1.7% (27/1,602), with the highest burden in children aged 0–5 years (3.6%) and peak circulation in winter and spring; a genotype shift occurred from A2.2.2 in 2024 to B2 in 2025 (12/12 vs. [10.3389/fmicb.2026.1915595]

The review concludes that hMPV is a leading cause of both upper and lower respiratory tract infections globally. It highlights the absence of licensed vaccines or specific antiviral therapies, with supportive care remaining the primary management strategy. [10.3329/jmomc.v11i2.90296]
Among 309 infants, 190 (61.5%) were male and 42 (13.6%) were classified as severe cases. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10485146/v1]

news.headline_en: Self-Sampling Feasibility Confirmed for Respiratory Infections.
news.lead_en: A pilot study in Swiss households found self-sampling to be feasible for respiratory infections, including human metapneumovirus.
key_findings_en: 63% of index case samples were positive for any of the 13 respiratory viruses tested, including human metapneumovirus.
Potential within-household transmission of human metapneumovirus was observed.
The study highlights the viability of decentralized surveillance but notes limitations such as missing samples and lack of bacterial pathogen testing.
news.trend_or_risk_en: Human metapneumovirus may pose household transmission risks, but its specific role requires further research.
news.caveats_en: The study relied on self-sampling, which may introduce sampling bias and detection limitations.
news.brief_en: A pilot study conducted in 108 Swiss households from May to September 2023 explored the feasibility of self-sampling for respiratory infections, including human metapneumovirus. Participants collected nasal swabs for testing and used online questionnaires to report symptoms. The study found that 63% of index case samples were positive for any of the 13 respiratory viruses tested, with human metapneumovirus being one of them. Potential within-household transmission was observed for several viruses, including human metapneumovirus. The study, published online on July 29, 2026, in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases, highlighted the viability of decentralized surveillance but noted limitations such as missing samples and the absence of bacterial pathogen testing.

papers.title: No Cross-Infection between Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Human Metapneumovirus in a Shared Sick-Child Care Setting: A Prospective Observational Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background A simultaneous outbreak of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) occurred in Ube, Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan, from January to April 2025. Both viruses belong to the family Pneumoviridae and cause clinically similar respiratory illnesses in children. Whether sharing a care room between RSV-infected and hMPV-infected children leads to cross-infection has not been previously investigated. Methods Children aged 11 months to 11 years who tested positive for RSV or hMPV by rapid antigen tests at Suzuki Pediatric Clinic were enrolled in the sick-child care facility of the same clinic. RSV-positive and hMPV-positive children were cared for in the same room. Cross-infection was prospectively monitored for 1 to 4 months after discharge. Results A total of 54 children participated (RSV: 22, hMPV: 32; male: 31, female: 23; median age: 3 years, range: 11 months to 11 years). Shared care was conducted over 23 sessions from January to April 2025, with 2 to 7 children per session in rooms measuring 10.4 to 22.4 m2. No cross-infection was observed during the 1- to 3-month follow-up period. One RSV-infected infant (aged 11 months) subsequently developed hMPV infection 21 days after discharge; however, given that this interval exceeds the known incubation period of hMPV (3–6 days), this case was considered a community-acquired infection. Conclusion Shared sick-child care of RSV- and hMPV-infected children did not result in cross-infection over a follow-up period of 1 to 3 months. Viral interference, possibly mediated by the innate immune response including interferon induction, may explain this finding. Shared-room care of children with RSV and hMPV may be a safe and practical option for sick-child care facilities during co-epidemic periods.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether cross-infection occurs between respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in a shared sick-child care setting, addressing a gap in understanding the transmission dynamics of these viruses in clinical environments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective observational study was conducted at Suzuki Pediatric Clinic in Ube, Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan, from January to April 2025. Children aged 11 months to 11 years who tested positive for RSV or hMPV were enrolled in the shared sick-child care facility.
analysis.methods: RSV-positive and hMPV-positive children were placed in the same care room, and cross-infection was monitored prospectively for 1 to 4 months after discharge using clinical observations and follow-up testing.
analysis.main_results: A total of 54 children participated (RSV: 22, hMPV: 32). No cross-infection was observed during the 1- to 3-month follow-up period. One RSV-infected infant developed hMPV infection 21 days after discharge, but this was considered a community-acquired infection due to the interval exceeding the known incubation period of hMPV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that shared sick-child care for RSV- and hMPV-infected children does not lead to cross-infection, suggesting that viral interference, possibly through the innate immune response, may explain the lack of transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that shared sick-child care for RSV- and hMPV-infected children may be a safe and practical option during co-epidemic periods, potentially informing public health strategies for managing viral outbreaks in pediatric care settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its observational design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong given the direct monitoring of cross-infection over a follow-up period and the exclusion of community-acquired cases from the analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether cross-infection occurs between respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in a shared sick-child care setting in Japan. A total of 54 children, aged 11 months to 11 years, were enrolled in the facility from January to April 2025. No cross-infection was observed during the 1- to 3-month follow-up period. One RSV-infected infant developed hMPV infection 21 days after discharge, but this was attributed to community acquisition rather than transmission within the facility. The authors concluded that shared care for RSV- and hMPV-infected children does not result in cross-infection, possibly due to viral interference. These findings suggest that shared sick-child care may be a safe and practical option during co-epidemic periods. papers.title_zh: 在共享病童护理环境中呼吸道合胞病毒和 人偏肺病毒 之间没有交叉感染:一项前瞻性观察研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background A simultaneous outbreak of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) occurred in Ube, Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan, from January to April 2025. Both viruses belong to the family Pneumoviridae and cause clinically similar respiratory illnesses in children. Whether sharing a care room between RSV-infected and hMPV-infected children leads to cross-infection has not been previously investigated. Methods Children aged 11 months to 11 years who tested positive for RSV or hMPV by rapid antigen tests at Suzuki Pediatric Clinic were enrolled in the sick-child care facility of the same clinic. RSV-positive and hMPV-positive children were cared for in the same room. Cross-infection was prospectively monitored for 1 to 4 months after discharge. Results A total of 54 children participated (RSV: 22, hMPV: 32; male: 31, female: 23; median age: 3 years, range: 11 months to 11 years). Shared care was conducted over 23 sessions from January to April 2025, with 2 to 7 children per session in rooms measuring 10.4 to 22.4 m2. No cross-infection was observed during the 1- to 3-month follow-up period. One RSV-infected infant (aged 11 months) subsequently developed hMPV infection 21 days after discharge; however, given that this interval exceeds the known incubation period of hMPV (3–6 days), this case was considered a community-acquired infection. Conclusion Shared sick-child care of RSV- and hMPV-infected children did not result in cross-infection over a follow-up period of 1 to 3 months. Viral interference, possibly mediated by the innate immune response including interferon induction, may explain this finding. Shared-room care of children with RSV and hMPV may be a safe and practical option for sick-child care facilities during co-epidemic periods.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 2025 年 1 月至 4 月,日本山口县宇部市同时发生了呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 人偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 的 暴发 病毒。这两种病毒均属于肺病毒科,会引起临床上相似的儿童呼吸道疾病。此前尚未研究过 RSV 感染者和 hMPV 感染者共用一间护理室是否会导致交叉感染。方法将在铃木儿科诊所快速抗原检测检测出 RSV 或 hMPV 阳性的 11 个月至 11 岁儿童纳入该诊所的病童护理机构。RSV 阳性和 hMPV 阳性儿童在同一房间接受护理。出院后1至4个月前瞻性监测交叉感染。结果 共有 54 名儿童参与(RSV:22,hMPV:32;男性:31,女性:23;中位年龄:3 岁,范围:11 个月至 11 岁)。2025 年 1 月至 4 月期间,共进行了 23 次共享护理,每次护理 2 至 7 名儿童,房间面积为 10.4 至 22.4 平方米。随访1~3个月未发现交叉感染。一名 RSV 感染婴儿(11 个月大)随后在出院 21 天后出现 hMPV 感染;然而,考虑到这一间隔超过了已知的 hMPV 潜伏期(3-6 天),该病例被认为是社区获得性感染。结论 在 1 至 3 个月的随访期内,RSV 和 hMPV 感染儿童的共同病童护理并未导致交叉感染。病毒干扰可能是由先天 免疫应答 介导的,包括干扰素诱导,可以解释这一发现。在共流行期间,对感染 RSV 和 hMPV 的儿童进行共用房间护理可能是患病儿童护理机构的一种安全实用的选择。

papers.title: Clinical characteristics and factors associated with severe disease in hospitalized infants with human metapneumovirus pneumonia and respiratory bacterial co-detection: a single-center retrospective study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is an important cause of lower respiratory tract infection in infants, but data on infants with respiratory bacterial co-detection are limited. We aimed to describe the clinical and microbiological characteristics of this population and to explore factors associated with severe disease. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective study of infants aged 12 months or younger who were hospitalized at Henan Children's Hospital between October 2024 and March 2025 with hMPV pneumonia and clinically adjudicated respiratory bacterial co-detection. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, imaging, treatment, and 6-month follow-up data were extracted from medical records. Severe disease was classified according to the pediatric community-acquired pneumonia guideline and the discharge diagnosis. Group comparisons used chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and the Mann–Whitney U test. Exploratory logistic regression was performed; the primary model excluded lethargy because it overlapped with severity criteria, and a secondary warning-sign model included lethargy. Results Among 309 infants, 190 (61.5%) were male and 42 (13.6%) were classified as severe cases. Streptococcus pneumoniae was the most frequently co-detected bacterium. Among 143 infants who underwent chest CT, multilobar pneumonia (90.9%) and ground-glass opacity (56.6%) were the most common findings. In the primary exploratory model, artificial feeding (OR 2.60, 95% CI 1.27–5.34), underlying diseases (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.14–5.21), and lower albumin levels (OR 0.85 per 1 g/L increase, 95% CI 0.78–0.94) were associated with severe disease. In the secondary model, lethargy was strongly associated with severe presentation (OR 5.02, 95% CI 2.38–10.62) and should be interpreted as a warning sign rather than an independent causal factor. Conclusions Underlying diseases, artificial feeding, and lower albumin levels may help identify infants with hMPV pneumonia and respiratory bacterial co-detection who require closer monitoring. Lethargy should be regarded as an early warning sign. These association-based findings require confirmation in multicenter prospective studies with standardized pathogen quantification and adjudication.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Background Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is an important cause of lower respiratory tract infection in infants, but data on infants with respiratory bacterial co-detection are limited. We aimed to describe the clinical and microbiological characteristics of this population and to explore factors associated with severe disease. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective study of infants aged 12 months or younger who were hospitalized at Henan Children's Hospital between October 2024 and March 2025 with hMPV pneumonia and clinically adjudicated respiratory bacterial co-detection. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, imaging, treatment, and 6-month follow-up data were extracted from medical records. Severe disease was classified according to the pediatric community-acquired pneumonia guideline and the discharge diagnosis. Group comparisons used chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and the Mann–Whitney U test. Exploratory logistic regression was performed; the primary model excluded lethargy because it overlapped with severity criteria, and a secondary warning-sign model included lethargy. Results Among 309 infants, 190 (61.5%) were male and 42 (13.6%) were classified as severe cases. Streptococcus pneumoniae was the most frequently co-detected bacterium. Among 143 infants who underwent chest CT, multilobar pneumonia (90.9%) and ground-glass opacity (56.6%) were the most common findings. In the primary exploratory model, artificial feeding (OR 2.60, 95% CI 1.27–5.34), underlying diseases (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.14–5.21), and lower albumin levels (OR 0.85 per 1 g/L increase, 95% CI 0.78–0.94) were associated with severe disease. In the secondary model, lethargy was strongly associated with severe presentation (OR 5.02, 95% CI 2.38–10.62) and should be interpreted as a warning sign rather than an independent causal factor. Conclusions Underlying diseases, artificial feeding, and lower albumin levels may help identify infants with hMPV pneumonia and respiratory bacterial co-detection who require closer monitoring. Lethargy should be regarded as an early warning sign. These association-based findings require confirmation in multicenter prospective studies with standardized pathogen quantification and adjudication.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics and factors associated with severe disease in hospitalized infants with human metapneumovirus (hMPV) pneumonia and respiratory bacterial co-detection. Conducted as a single-center retrospective study at Henan Children's Hospital between October 2024 and March 2025, the research included 309 infants, of whom 42 were classified as severe cases. However, the study emphasizes the need for confirmation in multicenter prospective studies with standardized pathogen quantification and adjudication.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 基础疾病、人工喂养和较低的白蛋白水平可能有助于识别患有 hMPV 肺炎和呼吸道细菌共检测的婴儿,这些婴儿需要更密切的监测。嗜睡应被视为早期预警信号。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些基于关联的发现需要通过标准化病原体定量和判定进行多中心前瞻性研究的确认。提供的证据没有报告具体的统计功效或细菌联合检测的确切数量。

papers.title: Human Metapneumovirus as an Emerging Respiratory Pathogen: A Comprehensive Review
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) has emerged as a significant pathogen responsible for a wide spectrum of respiratory illnesses across all age groups, with the greatest burden observed in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Since its discovery in 2001, extensive research has revealed its epidemiology, clinical manifestations, modes of transmission, and impact on public health. It is now recognized as a leading cause of both upper and lower respiratory tract infections. Despite significant advances in diagnostic technologies—particularly nucleic acid amplification methods such as RT-PCR—and a growing understanding of the virology and immune response, no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral therapy is currently available. Supportive care remains the mainstay of management. Co-infections with hMPV and other respiratory pathogens, such as RSV or SARS-CoV, present additional challenges and may complicate disease severity. Moreover, the limited understanding of hMPV immunopathogenesis, particularly in vulnerable populations, emphasizes the necessity for further research. In conclusion, hMPV represents an important target for future therapeutic and preventive interventions. With ongoing research and development, especially in vaccine design and antiviral therapy, there is hope for reducing the global disease burden of hMPV and improving outcomes for those most at risk. Journal of Monno Medical College December, 2025;11(2):141-149

Since its discovery in 2001, extensive research has revealed its epidemiology, clinical manifestations, modes of transmission, and impact on public health. It is now recognized as a leading cause of both upper and lower respiratory tract infections. Despite significant advances in diagnostic technologies—particularly nucleic acid amplification methods such as RT-PCR—and a growing understanding of the virology and immune response, no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral therapy is currently available. Supportive care remains the mainstay of management. Co-infections with hMPV and other respiratory pathogens, such as RSV or SARS-CoV, present additional challenges and may complicate disease severity. Moreover, the limited understanding of hMPV immunopathogenesis, particularly in vulnerable populations, emphasizes the necessity for further research. In conclusion, hMPV represents an important target for future therapeutic and preventive interventions. With ongoing research and development, especially in vaccine design and antiviral therapy, there is hope for reducing the global disease burden of hMPV and improving outcomes for those most at risk. Journal of Monno Medical College December, 2025;11(2):141-149

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines Human metapneumovirus (hMPV; Metapneumovirus hominis) as a respiratory pathogen, focusing on its disease spectrum, affected host populations, and the central question of its public health impact and management gaps. The scope explicitly targets human infection and disease across all age groups, with emphasis on infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis without explicit systematic review methods, databases, or eligibility criteria reported. It synthesizes findings from studies identified through unspecified search strategies, with no meta-analysis or pooled estimates provided.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that hMPV is a leading cause of both upper and lower respiratory tract infections globally. It highlights the absence of licensed vaccines or specific antiviral therapies, with supportive care remaining the primary management strategy.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Key gaps include the limited understanding of hMPV immunopathogenesis, particularly in vulnerable populations such as immunocompromised individuals. Additionally, the review notes challenges posed by co-infections with other respiratory pathogens, which may complicate disease severity and management.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the urgent need for research into hMPV immunopathogenesis and the development of vaccines and antiviral therapies. It also underscores the importance of improved diagnostic tools and surveillance systems to better understand and mitigate the global disease burden of hMPV.

analysis.summary_en: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is recognized as a significant respiratory pathogen causing a broad spectrum of illnesses across all age groups, with the highest burden in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Since its discovery in 2001, research has advanced understanding of its epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and transmission, yet no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral therapy exists, leaving supportive care as the mainstay of treatment. hMPV is now established as a leading cause of both upper and lower respiratory tract infections. Key gaps persist in the understanding of its immunopathogenesis, particularly in vulnerable populations, and challenges arise from co-infections with other respiratory pathogens. Future priorities include targeted research into immunopathogenesis, development of vaccines and antiviral therapies, and enhancement of diagnostic and surveillance systems to reduce the global disease burden.

papers.abstract_zh: 人偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 已成为导致所有年龄段的多种呼吸道疾病的重要病原体,其中在婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下的个体中观察到的负担最大。自2001年发现以来,广泛的研究揭示了其流行病学、临床表现、传播的模式以及对公众健康的影响。现在它被认为是鞋面和 下呼吸道感染 的主要原因。尽管诊断技术(尤其是 RT-PCR 等核酸扩增方法)取得了重大进展,并且对病毒学和 免疫应答 的了解不断加深,但目前尚无获得许可的 疫苗 或特定的 抗病毒药物 疗法。支持性护理仍然是管理的支柱。hMPV 和 RSV 或 SARS-CoV 等其他呼吸道病原体的共同感染带来了额外的挑战,并可能使疾病的严重程度变得复杂化。此外,对 hMPV 免疫发病机制的了解有限,特别是在易感人群中,强调了进一步研究的必要性。总之,hMPV 代表了未来治疗和预防干预的重要目标。随着持续的研究和开发,特别是 疫苗 设计和 抗病毒药物 治疗,有望减轻 hMPV 的全球疾病负担并改善高危人群的预后。莫诺医学院学报,2025 年 12 月;11(2):141-149

papers.title: Longitudinal Outcomes and Ribavirin Use in Lung Transplant Recipients with Respiratory Syncytial Virus or Human Metapneumovirus Infection: A Real-World Multicenter Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) are clinically relevant pathogens in lung transplant (LT) recipients, but their impact on lung function and the benefit of ribavirin remains uncertain. We conducted a prospective multicenter observational cohort study of adult LT recipients with RSV or hMPV infection diagnosed between 2021 and 2024 at five centers, with follow-up for up to 12 months. Ribavirin was prescribed at the treating physician’s discretion. Multivariable analysis assessed the association between ribavirin and percentage change in forced expiratory volume in the first second (FEV1) at 90 days, using FEV1 three months before infection as baseline and adjusting for baseline FEV1, pre-existing chronic lung allograft dysfunction, and time since transplantation. Seventy-six patients were included; 60 (78.9%) had RSV and 16 (21.1%) hMPV. Lower respiratory tract infection occurred in 48.7%, and an acute ≥10% FEV1 decline at 14 days was observed in 29.3%. Among patients with lower respiratory tract infection, 45.9% received corticosteroids alone and 37.8% corticosteroids plus ribavirin. No statistically significant between-group differences in allograft dysfunction or mortality were observed. RSV and hMPV infections after LT were frequently associated with lower respiratory involvement and lung function decline. In this observational cohort, ribavirin use was not independently associated with 90-day FEV1 change; however, residual confounding and limited statistical power preclude conclusions regarding treatment efficacy.

It is a multicenter observational cohort study involving 76 patients with RSV or hMPV infections diagnosed between 2021 and 2024. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和人偏肺病毒(hMPV)是肺移植(LT)受者的临床相关病原体,但它们对肺功能和利巴韦林的益处的影响仍不确定。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们开展了一项前瞻性多中心观察性队列研究,纳入2021年至2024年间在五个中心诊断为RSV或hMPV感染的成年肺移植受者,随访时间长达12个月。共纳入76名患者;其中60名(78.9%)为RSV感染,16名(21.1%)为hMPV感染。
elements_zh.methods: 多变量分析评估了利巴韦林与 90 天第一秒用力呼气量 (FEV1) 百分比变化之间的关联,使用感染前三个月的 FEV1 作为基线,并根据基线 FEV1、预先存在的慢性同种异体肺移植功能障碍和移植后时间进行调整。
elements_zh.main_results: 48.7% 的患者发生 下呼吸道感染,29.3% 的患者在 14 天时出现急性 ≥10% FEV1 下降。在 下呼吸道感染 患者中,45.9% 单独接受皮质类固醇治疗,37.8% 接受皮质类固醇加利巴韦林治疗。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调了 LT 后 RSV 和 hMPV 感染与下呼吸道受累和肺功能下降的频繁关联。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,LT 受者的 RSV 和 hMPV 感染是重要的临床事件,需要监测呼吸道并发症。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在这项观察性 队列研究 中,利巴韦林的使用与 90 天 FEV1 变化并不独立相关;然而,残留的混杂因素和有限的统计功效排除了有关 治疗 功效的结论。

papers.title: Genotype turnover and global evolutionary dynamics of G gene duplication variants in human metapneumovirus: insights from prospective surveillance in Nantong, China, 2024–2025
papers.abstract: Background Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a leading cause of acute respiratory infections worldwide, yet whole-genome surveillance data remain scarce in eastern China. The evolutionary dynamics of G gene duplication variants and their molecular drivers are poorly characterized. Methods From 2024 to 2025, we conducted prospective hMPV surveillance in Nantong, Jiangsu Province, screening 1,602 respiratory specimens by multiplex qPCR. Complete whole-genome sequences were obtained from 26 of 27 positive strains via probe-capture next-generation sequencing, and integrated with 574 global reference genomes. G gene duplication variants (111nt_dup/180nt_dup) were characterized, O-glycosylation sites predicted (NetOGlyc 4.0), and Bayesian phylodynamic analysis (BEAST v1.10.4) performed on the 111nt_dup lineage. Results The overall detection rate was 1.7% (27/1,602), with the highest burden in children aged 0–5 years (3.6%) and peak circulation in winter and spring. Phylogenetic analysis revealed a sharp genotype shift among the sequenced strains—from A2.2.2 in 2024 to B2 in 2025 (12/12 vs. 0/14; p 90% by 2025 (Cochran-Armitage trend test, p = 6.86 × 10 −7 ), whereas 180nt_dup disappeared after 2021. The 111nt_dup lineage displayed near-complete fixation of serine at G protein position 90 (S90, 98.9% vs. 0% in 180nt_dup; p 0.95). Bayesian Skyline analysis showed a pandemic-associated population bottleneck (2020–2021) followed by rapid recovery to pre-pandemic levels by late 2022. Conclusion The global dominance of 111nt_dup is better explained by lineage-specific molecular selection than neutral drift. Co-occurrence of the 111nt_dup with the predicted S90 O-glycosylation site suggests a model in which predicted glycosylation-driven optimization of the G protein mucin-like domain may enhance fitness, with implications for hMPV vaccine strain surveillance.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 人偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 是全球急性呼吸道感染的主要原因,但完整的 基因组 监测 数据在中国东部仍然稀缺。G 基因重复变异的进化动力学及其分子驱动因素的特征尚不清楚。方法 2024年至2025年,我们在江苏省南通市进行了前瞻性hMPV 监测,通过多重qPCR筛查了1,602份呼吸道标本。通过探针捕获下一代测序从 27 个阳性菌株中的 26 个获得完整的 基因组 序列,并与 574 个全球参考 基因组 进行整合。对 G 基因重复变异 (111nt_dup/180nt_dup) 进行了表征,预测了 O-糖基化位点 (NetOGlyc 4.0),并对 111nt_dup 谱系进行了贝叶斯系统动力学分析 (BEAST v1.10.4)。结果 总体检出率为1.7%(27/1,602),其中0~5岁儿童负担最高(3.6%),循环高峰期为冬春季节。系统发育分析揭示了测序菌株之间的急剧基因型转变——从2024年的A2.2.2到2025年的B2(12/12 vs. 0/14;到2025年p为90%(Cochran-Armitage趋势检验,p = 6.86 × 10 -7 ),而180nt_dup在2021年后消失。111nt_dup 谱系显示丝氨酸在 G 蛋白位置 90 处几乎完全固定(S90,180nt_dup 中为 98.9% vs. 0%;p = 0.95)。贝叶斯天际线分析显示,出现了与大流行相关的人口瓶颈(2020-2021 年),随后到 2022 年底迅速恢复到大流行前的水平。结论 111nt_dup 的全球主导地位谱系特异性分子选择比中性漂移更好地解释了 111nt_dup 与预测的 S90 O-糖基化位点的共现,这表明预测的 G 蛋白粘蛋白样结构域的糖基化驱动优化可能会增强适应性,这对 hMPV 疫苗 菌株 监测 具有影响。

papers.title_original: Specific Clinical Characteristics of Severe Viral Pneumonia in Children: A Comparative Study Based on Six Common Respiratory Viruses

analysis.research_question_and_background: Severe viral pneumonia (SVP) is a leading cause of childhood morbidity, yet comparative clinical characteristics across common respiratory viruses remain insufficiently defined. The study addressed the knowledge gap by characterizing and comparing six frequently detected viruses in pediatric SVP to inform differential diagnosis and management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective comparative study enrolled 450 children hospitalized with SVP across multiple centers. Participants were stratified into six groups based on the detected respiratory virus: human adenovirus (n=184), human rhinovirus (n=131), respiratory syncytial virus (n=53), human bocavirus (n=30), human parainfluenza virus (n=26), and human metapneumovirus (n=26).
analysis.methods: Respiratory pathogens were identified using target next-generation sequencing (t-NGS). Clinical characteristics, imaging features, and epidemiological data were systematically compared among the six virus groups using standardized protocols.
analysis.main_results: The age distribution differed significantly across the six virus groups (p<0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provides comparative evidence that age distribution varies by viral etiology in pediatric SVP, highlighting potential age-specific risk profiles for different respiratory viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform targeted surveillance strategies and clinical protocols for pediatric SVP by identifying age-associated risk patterns linked to specific viral pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The retrospective design and single-center setting limit generalizability, and the absence of randomization and control groups reduces causal inference strength, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study enrolled 450 children hospitalized with severe viral pneumonia (SVP) to compare clinical characteristics across six respiratory viruses using target next-generation sequencing (t-NGS). The age distribution differed significantly among groups (p<0.001), with human metapneumovirus representing 26 cases. The study interprets these findings as evidence of age-specific risk profiles for different viral etiologies in pediatric SVP. The results suggest potential utility for targeted surveillance and clinical protocols, though retrospective design and single-center limitations reduce generalizability and causal inference, warranting moderate confidence.

papers.title: Respiratory Viral Detection and Invasive Bacterial Infections in Infants ≤90 Days.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Comprehensive data are needed to guide the use and interpretation of molecular respiratory viral testing in evaluating infants 0 to ≤90 days old for invasive bacterial infections (IBIs). We aimed to describe the frequency and severity of respiratory viral infections in febrile and nonfebrile infants 0 to ≤90 days of age with emergency department visits or hospitalizations for acute respiratory illness and to quantify the occurrence of IBI (bacteremia and bacterial meningitis) in these groups. METHODS: The New Vaccine Surveillance Network conducts acute respiratory illness surveillance at 7 US pediatric medical institutions in the United States. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of febrile and nonfebrile infants 0 to ≤90 days of age enrolled in the emergency department or inpatient hospital settings. Respiratory viral detection from research respiratory samples in the context of clinical severity and IBI was examined. RESULTS: Three thousand seven hundred and eighty febrile and nonfebrile infants 0 to ≤90 days of age enrolled from December 1, 2016, to March 31, 2020. Respiratory syncytial virus was the most common virus detected regardless of febrile status. IBIs were significantly more frequent in febrile infants without a respiratory virus compared with those with a respiratory virus detected (4.9% vs. IBIs were not detected in infants with respiratory syncytial virus (n = 259), parainfluenza virus (n = 66), human metapneumovirus (n = 13), influenza virus (n = 67), or adenovirus (n = 11) alone. IBI and respiratory viral coinfections were found in infants with endemic coronaviruses (5.8%, 3/52), rhinovirus/enterovirus (2.2%, 7/324) and viral coinfections (2.0%, 2/99). CONCLUSIONS: These data suggest that febrile infants 0 to ≤90 days old with certain respiratory viruses are at lower risk of IBI.

news.content: Medscape AI News & Perspective Tools & Reference CME/CE More NEW! Ask complex medical questions and find the latest clinical guidance for drugs & conditions with Medscape AI× EN RegisterLog In AI Mode Medscape News UK Medbrief Self-Sampling Can Be Feasible for Detecting Respiratory Infections Edited by Devyani Gholap August 10, 2026 0 Add to Email Alerts TOPLINE In a pilot study of 108 Swiss households, participants self-collected samples during respiratory illness. Valid results were obtained for 70% of expected human samples and 51% of pet samples, supporting the feasibility of remote household-based surveillance for respiratory infections. METHODOLOGY Researchers conducted a pilot study to evaluate whether household members could collect their own respiratory samples for testing and whether online symptom questionnaires plus telemedicine could support decentralised surveillance. They enrolled 108 households, including 161 adults, 32 children, 29 cats, and 15 dogs, in Switzerland from May to September 2023. The first household member to develop new respiratory symptoms (sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, cough, or shortness of breath) for at least 24 hours collected a nasal swab as the index case; other members collected swabs 7 days later. All samples were mailed to a central biobank. Samples were tested using a multiplex polymerase chain reaction panel for 13 common respiratory viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, human rhinovirus, human respiratory syncytial virus, human metapneumovirus, and human parainfluenza virus. A short survey was conducted to assess the clarity of instructions and acceptability. The total duration of the study was 21 months. TAKEAWAY Overall, 70% (131/188) of samples from index cases, 69% (105/152) of samples from household contacts, and 51% (24/47) of samples from pets were analysed. Swabs from symptomatic participants were positive far more often than those from asymptomatic participants (60% vs 6%); potential within-household transmission was observed for rhinovirus (14 cases), SARS-CoV-2 (three cases), and parainfluenza (two cases). Among index cases, 63% of samples were positive for any of the 13 viruses, most commonly rhinovirus and SARS-CoV-2; among human household contacts, 23% were positive for any virus, with rhinovirus predominating. In the survey, 70% of respondents said the nasal swab was not unpleasant, and 52% said the nasal swab was not unpleasant for the pet; among participants from 10 households who became ill during the first month, 80% reported that telemedicine consultations were helpful. IN PRACTICE "It is feasible to establish a decentralized household-based cohort for pandemic preparedness using remote sampling and online questionnaires. Our study will inform investigations of emerging diseases," the authors wrote. SOURCE The study was led by Karin Grimm, MD, Bern University Hospital, University of Bern, Bern, Switzerland. It was published online on July 29, 2026, as a short communication in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. LIMITATIONS About one third of the expected samples were missing, and the study did not test for bacterial pathogens such as pneumococcus and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. DISCLOSURES The study was funded by the Multidisciplinary Center for Infectious Diseases at the University of Bern. The authors reported having no competing interests. SUGGESTED FOR YOU This article was created using several editorial tools, including AI, as part of the process. Human editors reviewed this content before publication. 0 References References Grimm K, Hodel EM, Gasser L, et al. Feasibility of studying respiratory infection transmission in a Swiss household cohort: Findings from the BEready ("Bern, get ready") study. Int J Infect Dis. analysis.time: The study was conducted from May to September 2023, with results published online on July 29, 2026. The first symptoms were reported during the first month of the study.
analysis.location_and_population: The study was conducted in 108 households in Switzerland, including 161 adults, 32 children, 29 cats, and 15 dogs.
analysis.event: A pilot study evaluated the feasibility of self-sampling for respiratory infections, including human metapneumovirus, in a Swiss household cohort. The study involved participants collecting nasal swabs for testing and using online questionnaires to report symptoms.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Among index cases, 63% of samples were positive for any of the 13 respiratory viruses, with human metapneumovirus being one of the tested pathogens. Potential within-household transmission was observed for human metapneumovirus (as part of the broader respiratory viruses tested).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was published as a short communication in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. It reported the feasibility of decentralized household-based surveillance for respiratory infections, including human metapneumovirus, but noted limitations such as missing samples and lack of testing for bacterial pathogens.

analysis.brief_en: A pilot study conducted in 108 Swiss households from May to September 2023 explored the feasibility of self-sampling for respiratory infections, including human metapneumovirus. Participants collected nasal swabs for testing, and online questionnaires were used to report symptoms. The study found that 63% of index case samples were positive for any of the 13 respiratory viruses tested, with human metapneumovirus being one of them. Potential within-household transmission was observed for several viruses, including human metapneumovirus. The study, published online on July 29, 2026, in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases, highlighted the viability of decentralized surveillance but noted limitations such as missing samples and the absence of bacterial pathogen testing. The findings support the use of remote sampling and telemedicine for pandemic preparedness, though further research is needed to confirm the specific role of human metapneumovirus in transmission and disease.
analysis.summary_en: A pilot study conducted in 108 Swiss households from May to September 2023 explored the feasibility of self-sampling for respiratory infections, including human metapneumovirus. Participants collected nasal swabs for testing, and online questionnaires were used to report symptoms. The study found that 63% of index case samples were positive for any of the 13 respiratory viruses tested, with human metapneumovirus being one of them. Potential within-household transmission was observed for several viruses, including human metapneumovirus. news.source_body_en: A pilot study conducted in 108 Swiss households from May to September 2023 explored the feasibility of self-sampling for respiratory infections, including human metapneumovirus. Participants collected nasal swabs for testing, and online questionnaires were used to report symptoms. The study found that 63% of index case samples were positive for any of the 13 respiratory viruses tested, with human metapneumovirus being one of them. Potential within-household transmission was observed for several viruses, including human metapneumovirus. The study, published online on July 29, 2026, in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases, highlighted the viability of decentralized surveillance but noted limitations such as missing samples and the absence of bacterial pathogen testing. The findings support the use of remote sampling and telemedicine for pandemic preparedness, though further research is needed to confirm the specific role of human metapneumovirus in transmission and disease.

Q&A: Which Hospitalized Children With RTIs Face the Highest Severe Disease Risk? By Lorraine L. Janeczko, MPH - Last Updated: August 7, 2026 Maria Deza Leon, MD More than one in five children hospitalized with acute respiratory tract infections (RTIs) develop severe disease, and children transferred from a referring hospital face the highest risk, according to a retrospective study conducted at two Canadian pediatric centers. “In this cohort study of hospitalized children with acute RTIs, many developed severe illness requiring intensive interventions. Chronic conditions were associated with increased risk, whereas viral coinfections were common but not associated with disease severity,” lead author Haifa Mtaweh, MD, PhD, of The Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto, Ontario, and her coauthors wrote in JAMA Network Open. “Despite low mortality, the complication burden remained high, underscoring the need for targeted prevention and ongoing surveillance.” Risk Factors for Severe Disease The 2,585 enrolled children (median age, 2.5 years) were hospitalized with acute RTIs between July 2022 and June 2023 at The Hospital for Sick Children and BC Children’s Hospital in Vancouver, British Columbia. Roughly half (50.6%) had at least one chronic condition, with neurologic, developmental, or genetic diagnoses most common. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and enterovirus-rhinovirus were the predominant pathogens identified, at 30.4% and 25.6%, respectively. Severe illness, including cardiac arrest, the need for noninvasive or invasive ventilation, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), or kidney replacement therapy, occurred among 551 children (21.3%), and of these, 37 (6.7%) died. In multivariable analysis, children transferred from a referring hospital (adjusted risk ratio [aRR], 4.73; 95% CI, 4.01-5.59), children with a single identified virus compared with none (aRR, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.30-2.08), children with two or more chronic conditions compared with none (aRR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.36-1.93), and patients aged less than 1 year and more than 10 years were at increased risk for severe outcomes. Viral coinfections, detected among approximately 15% of patients, were not associated with severity. An Expert Shares Insights Maria Deza Leon, MD, a pediatric infectious disease physician at Children’s Mercy in Kansas City, Missouri, who was not involved in the study, spoke with Physician’s Weekly about the study and its implications for pediatric acute RTI care. Physician’s Weekly: Which complications should clinicians anticipate among children hospitalized with RTIs, and do these risks vary by viral pathogen? Dr. Deza Leon: Common severe complications included acute respiratory distress syndrome, cardiac complications, septic shock, pneumothorax, and empyema, with some children requiring ECMO or kidney replacement therapy. Although complication rates were generally similar across viruses, influenza was more often associated with ARDS and septic shock, whereas human metapneumovirus was more often associated with cardiac complications and extracorporeal support. These findings suggest that viral identification may help inform risk, but clinical management should remain focused on the patient’s overall trajectory. Which chronic conditions place patients at the highest risk for severe outcomes, and how can clinicians use this information to guide individualized care strategies? Children with neurologic, developmental, and genetic disorders carried the greatest risk for severe disease, with chronic pulmonary and cardiac conditions also associated with increased risk. Risk was highest among children with multiple chronic conditions, highlighting the impact of medical complexity on patient outcomes. Clinicians can use this information to identify high-risk patients early and guide management decisions. Children with complex medical conditions may benefit from closer monitoring, a lower threshold for escalation of care, and careful discharge planning. These findings also support prioritizing preventive measures, including routine immunizations, RSV prevention strategies when appropriate, and timely access to specialty care for medically complex children. What factors might explain why the highest risk concentrates in two groups—infants and older children/adolescents? This elevated risk among infants is not unexpected. Smaller airways, reduced physiologic reserve, and immature immune function make young children especially vulnerable to respiratory infections. The increased risk observed among older children and adolescents is particularly noteworthy. Although hospitalization for respiratory tract infections is less common in these age groups than in infancy, those requiring admission may represent a more medically complex population with underlying comorbidities or more severe illness at presentation. These findings suggest that while the overall burden of respiratory disease is highest in infancy, the potential severity of respiratory tract infections in hospitalized adolescents should not be overlooked. How does coinfection influence disease course and outcomes for these patients? One of the more reassuring findings was that viral coinfection did not appear to increase the risk of severe disease. Coinfections were relatively common, occurring in about 15% of cases, but their frequency was similar among children with severe and nonsevere illness. These findings suggest that detecting multiple respiratory viruses should not automatically be considered a predictor of worse outcomes. The study also highlights the challenges of interpreting highly sensitive molecular testing, which can detect residual viral nucleic acid that may not reflect active infection or meaningfully contribute to disease severity. What key insights does this study offer about identifying high‐risk patients, anticipating complications, and optimizing early supportive care? This study serves as an important reminder that severe respiratory infection remains a significant source of pediatric morbidity, even in the post-pandemic era. More than one in five hospitalized children met criteria for severe disease, and nearly one-quarter required pediatric ICU admission. The findings reinforce the importance of focusing on patient-specific risk factors rather than the viral diagnosis alone, with particular attention to children with medical complexity and multiple chronic conditions. Transfer from an outside hospital may also serve as a useful marker of greater illness severity. In addition, the results support continued use of preventive strategies, including vaccination and respiratory syncytial virus-targeted prevention when indicated. Clinicians should also remain alert for nonrespiratory complications, such as cardiac dysfunction and septic shock, particularly in children whose clinical status is worsening. Overall, although mortality was uncommon, the burden of severe illness, intensive care utilization, and associated complications remained substantial, underscoring the importance of early recognition, close monitoring, and aggressive supportive care. analysis.brief_en: A retrospective study conducted at two Canadian pediatric centers, The Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto and BC Children’s Hospital in Vancouver, analyzed 2,585 hospitalized children with acute respiratory tract infections (RTIs) between July 2022 and June 2023. The study found that more than one in five children developed severe disease, with those transferred from a referring hospital facing the highest risk. Chronic conditions, particularly neurologic, developmental, and genetic disorders, were strongly associated with increased severity. Viral coinfections were common but not linked to worse outcomes. Severe illness occurred in 21.3% of cases, with 6.7% of patients dying. The findings emphasize the importance of focusing on patient-specific risk factors rather than the viral pathogen alone, and highlight the need for targeted prevention and early supportive care for high-risk children. The study was published in JAMA Network Open, and its results suggest that clinicians should remain vigilant for nonrespiratory complications, such as cardiac dysfunction and septic shock, particularly in children with worsening clinical status.
